svg.title: Capture inbound headers
svg.desc: Two checkout requests, A and B, overlap in time. Each carries an X-Correlation-Id and an X-Box-Office header. A request filter reads both headers before checkout() runs and stores the values in that request's own duplicated context, so B's values never land in A's context. When checkout() reads its context, A gets 7f3a and web, and B gets c41e and kiosk.
svg.text: A request filter puts each request's headers in that request's duplicated context before checkout() runs.
Request A arrives at POST /checkout with X-Correlation-Id 7f3a and X-Box-Office web.
Routing has picked checkout(), but the request filter runs first and reads both headers.
The filter puts both values in A's duplicated context. Vert.x creates one for every request.
Request B arrives while checkout() is still running for A. The same filter reads B's headers.
B's values go into B's own duplicated context. A's context still holds 7f3a and web.
A's checkout() reads its context and gets 7f3a and web, not B's values.
B's checkout() reads c41e and kiosk from its own context.
The filter code and the keys are the same, but each request keeps its own values.
Sources: quarkus.io/guides/rest (request or response filters) and quarkus.io/guides/duplicated-context (context local data).
